phases.starting_model: COD 9010928 (Antao & Hassan 2007), C site reset to the centroid of its three O neighbours
COD 2311041 (Loopstra & Boldrini 1966, neutron), transformed to the conventional P2_1/n setting

phases_tested_and_rejected.evidence: Adding BaWO4 with its published cell held lowers wR from 7.294 to 7.069 and returns 2.7(2) wt%, but the chi-square gain is not located at BaWO4 reflections (22% of it falls in 35-39 deg, where scheelite has none) and its only reflection in a clear region, 200 at 32.2 deg, is no stronger than the background fluctuations at reflection-free positions.

A P-1 WO3 model fits marginally better (wR 7.14) but refines to alpha = 89.89, gamma = 90.05 deg, i.e. the triclinic metric is not supported; the gain comes from the different oxygen positions, not from the symmetry lowering.

weight_fraction_basis: normalised over the modelled crystalline phases (they are the only phases modelled; no amorphous or internal-standard scaling was applied)

weight_fraction_uncertainty.note: The quoted esd is the least-squares value only.  Repeating the refinement with other published WO3 and BaCO3 starting models, with/without preferred orientation and with different profile parameterisations moves the BaCO3 fraction over 0.50-0.54, so ~3 wt% is a realistic total uncertainty.  No micro-absorption (Brindley) correction was applied; both phases are strongly absorbing for Cu K-alpha.
